name: How much does a second-story addition cost per square foot in Los Angeles neighborhoods?

mainEntity.name: What is the realistic per-square-foot cost for a second-story addition in Los Angeles, Glendale, Pasadena, Burbank, and North Hollywood, including design, engineering, permits, and finishes?
mainEntity.text: What is the realistic per-square-foot cost for a second-story addition in Los Angeles, Glendale, Pasadena, Burbank, and North Hollywood, including design, engineering, permits, and finishes?

acceptedAnswer.text: A second-story addition in the Los Angeles area usually needs a budget that goes well beyond the framing and finish work alone. The true cost typically includes architectural plans, structural engineering, plan check, permits, demolition, roof removal, structural reinforcement, new stairs, electrical, plumbing, HVAC changes, insulation, drywall, flooring, and final finishes. Costs vary sharply by neighborhood, site access, and how much of the existing house must be upgraded to support the new level. In high-demand areas like Pasadena, Glendale, and Los Angeles proper, soft costs and inspection requirements can materially increase the total. Homeowners should compare full project budgets, not just per-square-foot construction numbers, because two similar-sized additions can differ greatly based on structural conditions and finish level. The most useful estimate is a range that separates hard construction costs from design and permitting so there are no surprises later.
acceptedAnswer.description: A second-story addition in Greater Los Angeles usually costs more than a ground-floor addition because the existing structure must be reinforced, the roof removed, and utilities extended. A realistic budget often includes design, structural engineering, permits, plan check fees, demolition, framing, MEP work, and finish selections, not just construction labor.
